title: Pandas basics
syllabusDesc: Load, inspect, and slice dataframes for quick analysis.
inlineSample:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
print(df.head())
desc: Use Pandas to read CSV/JSON data, inspect columns, filter rows, and select slices. Mastering the basics lets you explore data fast and build features for ML.
placeholder:
import pandas as pd
# load and inspect data here
solution:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
print(df.head())
print(df.describe())

challenges.title: Load and inspect
challenges.prompt: Load data.csv into a dataframe and print the first 3 rows.
challenges.starter:
import pandas as pd
# your code here
challenges.solution:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
print(df.head(3))

challenges.title: Filter rows
challenges.prompt: Print rows where the price column is greater than 100.
challenges.starter:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
# your code here
challenges.solution:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
print(df[df["price"] > 100])

challenges.title: Select columns
challenges.prompt: Print only the name and price columns from the dataframe.
challenges.starter:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
# your code here
challenges.solution:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
print(df[["name", "price"]])

challenges.title: Group and average
challenges.prompt: Group by category and print the average price per category.
challenges.starter:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
# your code here
challenges.solution:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
print(df.groupby("category")["price"].mean())

notes: Use df.copy() before mutating slices; set index if a column uniquely identifies rows. Start with small samples (head/tail) before heavy operations.
